messages:
alex: Quick heads-up: billing rollout confusion — need a tiny authoritative example of flag precedence. We had org+project+route+model set and some requests still hit the old behavior.

maria: Yup. Saw it live. Route override existed but only for a slice and the requests we tested fell outside that slice, so they used org-level behavior.

kevin: baseline rule I usually say: specificity wins (model > route > project > org). But runtime also supports a per-scope no-inherit toggle and audience-gated rules. Could be multiple interacting pieces.

sana: short checklist: 1) explicit no-inherit on a scope will block ancestors, 2) audience gating is evaluated when deciding if that scope's rule applies, 3) if a more-specific scope applies but is audience=false, a less-specific scope can win.

alex: example to be explicit: org=acme:true, project=acme/billing: (none), route=/api/v1/compute: override=false but audience=20%, model=gpt-lite:true. For a user not in the 20% the route override is not applied -> model or org may win depending on presence.

maria: runtime pseudocode we rely on today:
```
flags = collect_scoped_rules(request)  # returns list [(scope, value, block_inherit, audience_rule)]
apply_block_inherit(flags)            # remove ancestor entries blocked by descendants
for f in flags:                        # evaluate audience predicates, keep only matched ones
  if not evaluate_audience(f.audience_rule, request): drop f
return highest_specificity(flags)
```

kevin: important nuance: block_inherit only removes ancestor entries, it does NOT remove sibling/peer scopes. So a model setting with block_inherit removes the project/org ancestors, but not a separate route sibling unless that sibling is an ancestor.

sana: another gotcha we hit: if a route override has an implicit default (e.g., default=false) plus an audience gate, people assume the audience=true branch is the only thing that matters. But an explicit default still participates in resolution when audience=false. That caused the billing incident.

alex: action items: (A) emit a per-request compact resolution log line showing which scope produced the final value, and which audience predicates matched; (B) add a doc blurb called "Resolution & audience caveats"; (C) add a lint to catch suspicious route overrides.

kevin: I can add the log line. Proposed format: `flag_resolution: {flag_name, resolved_scope, resolved_value, matched_audiences}`. I'll make it structured but small.

maria: i will write the doc blurb. Draft sentence: "More specific scoped flags take precedence; audience gates are evaluated per-scoped-rule and can cause less-specific scopes to be selected if more-specific rules fail audience checks." Keep short.

sana: for linting: i suggest warning when a route override sets `default=false` and includes an audience rule without an explicit `fallback` defined. That pattern is what bit us.

kevin: i can add a CLI linter that runs on flag change PRs and on pre-commit. Will follow up with a tiny PR linking to the lint rule.

alex: also add a short unit-test pattern that simulates both matched and unmatched audience cases so the resolution doesn't regress.

maria: timeline: i'll publish the doc snippet today, kevin to add logs + linter PR by EOD, sana to add test cases in the flag-e2e harness tomorrow.

kevin: noted. i'll include sample log lines in the PR description so folks know how to query them in datadog.

alex: thanks team. marking this as checked-in. we'll monitor post-rollout. :thumbsup:
